heading: Threat model
body: `bare-url` is one of the addons Bare compiles into its binary, so every Bare process has it, sealed or not, and it inherits [Bare's threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md). The module's own [threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-url/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md), added in v2.5.5, says where it sits in that one. It parses and serializes WHATWG URLs through `liburl` and does not fetch, resolve, or open anything, so holding a `URL` reaches nothing. The risk is in the parser, which runs C code over strings an attacker chose. The module system uses URLs to name things and to pick a protocol, so an input whose scheme, host, origin, or path differs from what the WHATWG URL Standard says matters more than the parse itself suggests.
